home.title: Gay Hotels and Weekend Breaks in Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
home.description: Plan a gay weekend in Blackpool: men-only hotels, adults-only and gay-owned guest houses, rooms near Queen Street and the station, plus what is on nearby.
home.h1: Your gay weekend in Blackpool starts with the right room
home.intro: Choose where to sleep first, then build the weekend around it: gay hotels, guest houses and men-only stays within walking distance of the Rainbow Quarter.
home.body:
Blackpool does a gay weekend away better than most seaside towns, and the best ones start with a good base. Pick a room close to the Rainbow Quarter and the bars, the cabaret and the walk back are all sorted before you have packed a bag.

Why stay in or near the Rainbow Quarter?

The Rainbow Quarter is the LGBTQ+ district on Blackpool's North Shore, and its heart sits within a short stroll of most of the stays we list. From Funny Girls on Dickson Road, our listed stays are typically between two and five minutes away on foot, using the owner's measured walking times. Blackpool North station is about three minutes from Funny Girls.

That matters on a night out. You can drop your bags, go for tea, see a show, have a dance and be back in your room without needing a taxi, a tram timetable or a designated driver.

Types of stay

Not every trip is the same, so we sort stays by what you actually want from them.

  • Men-only hotels: adults-only accommodation for gay and bi men, some with a residents' bar.
  • Adults-only guest houses: smaller, quieter places for couples and friends.
  • Gay-owned guest houses: hosts who know the scene first-hand.
  • Hotels with a bar: a drink downstairs and a short climb to bed.
  • Near Queen Street: for late nights at the sharp end of the strip.
  • Near Blackpool North station: ideal for anyone coming in by rail.
  • Budget stays: spend less on the bed, more on the weekend.
  • Pride weekend hotels: rooms for the busiest weekend of the year.
  • Illuminations breaks: lights on the Prom by night, bars by the hotel.
  • Quiet midweek breaks: a calmer, cheaper trip away from the weekend crowds.

Prefer to browse the lot? The full stays directory has every gay and gay-friendly address in one place.

Tonight near your hotel

Once the key is in your pocket, the evening is easy to plan. Our short guides to the bars are written around where you are sleeping, and what is open tonight shows the places trading right now, based on listed hours. For cabaret, drag and one-off nights, check what is on.

Always confirm hours, prices and show times with the venue before you travel, because they change.

Plan the rest of the trip

Our trip-planning guides cover the practical bits: how to get there, how to put a weekend together and what to do for a first visit. If you are coming for the big weekend, read Blackpool Pride for visitors and book early.

Want to talk to other travellers? The community board is a friendly place to ask where to stay, where to eat and how to get home.

Looking after yourself and each other

Blackpool is a welcoming resort, and the council has backed a plan called Be Who You Want To Be to make the area safe for everyone. Even so, a good night out starts with a few habits: stay with your group, agree a meeting point, keep your phone charged and know how you are getting back.

If something goes wrong, read safety and getting back to your hotel for how to report hate crime and where to find local support. In an emergency, call 999.

Questions people ask

Where is the best place to stay for gay Blackpool?

Somewhere on or close to Lord Street, Dickson Road or Queen Street. You will be a few minutes on foot from the bars and shows.

Are there men-only hotels in Blackpool?

Yes. The Prince Albert Hotel on Yates Street and Trades Hotel on Lord Street both describe themselves as men-only and adults-only. See men-only hotels and confirm policies when you book.

Do I need a gay hotel to enjoy the scene?

No. Plenty of Blackpool hotels and guest houses are LGBTQ+ friendly. The advantage of a gay-run or gay-friendly place is a shared understanding and a short stroll home.

Can I walk from Blackpool North station?

Yes. The station is roughly two to three minutes from several of the Dickson Road venues and sits close to a number of the stays. See stays near the station.

When should I book for Pride?

As early as you can. Pride weekend is the busiest of the year, and the most popular places fill first. Details are on our Pride page.

Where can I read about the history of the scene?

For venue history, performers and support services, the owner's reference site rainbowquarter.co.uk goes into much more depth than we do here.

stays_hub.title: Where to Stay: Gay Hotels in Blackpool | Blackpool.gay
stays_hub.description: Every gay and gay-friendly hotel, guest house and men-only stay in Blackpool, sorted by type and distance from the Rainbow Quarter and the station.
stays_hub.h1: Where to stay: every gay and gay-friendly stay in Blackpool
stays_hub.intro: Browse gay hotels, guest houses and men-only stays in Blackpool, sorted by type and by how close they are to the bars and the station.
stays_hub.body:
Choosing where to stay is the biggest decision in a gay weekend in Blackpool. A room within walking distance of the Rainbow Quarter means you can enjoy the night and get home without fuss. Below is how to pick, then the full list.

How to choose a gay hotel in Blackpool

Start with what you want from the trip. A big night out suggests a base near Queen Street or Dickson Road. A romantic break might suit a quiet adults-only guest house. Travelling by train? Look near the station.

  • Men-only: hotels that welcome gay and bi men only. See men-only hotels.
  • Adults-only: no children, so a calmer atmosphere. See adults-only guest houses.
  • Gay-owned: run by hosts from the community. See gay-owned guest houses.
  • With a bar: a residents' or house bar on site. See hotels with a bar.
  • Location: near Queen Street or near Blackpool North station.

What does gay-friendly actually mean here?

It varies. Some places are explicitly gay or men-only, some belong to the local BAGS hoteliers group and welcome LGBTQ+ guests, and others simply have a good reputation. We say what each listing states about its policy, and we say when we could not confirm something.

Booking tips

Ask about check-in times and whether reception is staffed late, especially if your train is delayed. Some smaller places have stairs only, so ask if access matters to you. For Pride and the Illuminations, see Pride weekend hotels and Illuminations breaks, and book well ahead. If money is tight, try budget stays or a quiet midweek break.

Policies, facilities and prices change, so confirm them with the hotel before you pay.

Which area suits you?

Lord Street and Dickson Road put you close to the cabaret bars and Funny Girls, while stays around Queen Street suit people who plan to be out late. Rooms near the station make arriving and leaving simple, which is handy if you are coming by train for a short break.

If you are comparing options, think about what happens after midnight. A hotel with a residents' bar can mean one more drink without leaving the building, whereas a quiet guest house gives you an early night and a proper breakfast. Both are good, and which you pick depends on the trip.

Not sure? Ask on the community board, where other visitors share where they stayed, or read the safety guide for tips on getting back to your room.

pride.title: Blackpool Pride Weekend for Visitors | Blackpool.gay
pride.description: Planning Blackpool Pride? Facts on the 20th anniversary in 2026, the Lord Street street party, the parade route, and how to book your hotel early.
pride.h1: Blackpool Pride weekend: what visitors should know
pride.intro: Blackpool Pride is the biggest weekend of the LGBTQ+ calendar in the resort, so here is what happened in 2026 and how to plan your stay early.
pride.body:
Pride weekend turns the Rainbow Quarter into one big party, and rooms go quickly. Here is what we know, and what we do not yet.

Blackpool Pride 2026: the 20th anniversary

Blackpool Pride marked its 20th anniversary in 2026 with a three-day festival from 5 to 7 June, themed One Love, One Pride. The festival was based around the Blackpool Tower festival headland. Headline acts were Heather Small, 911 and the Cheeky Girls.

When is Blackpool Pride 2027?

We could not find announced dates for 2027 when we last checked, on 22 October 2026, so we are not guessing. The festival has been held in early June, so expect a similar slot. Check the official site at blackpoolpride.org for confirmed dates, and we will update this page.

The parade

In 2026 the parade set off at 11am on Saturday 6 June and followed the Promenade between Burlington Road West and Springfield Road. Route details can change from year to year, so check the official programme.

The Rainbow Quarter street party

Over two days, a free street party ran along Lord Street during the 2026 weekend, between Springfield Road and Cocker Street, organised with Blackpool Rainbow Alliance CIC and more than 20 local businesses. Gates opened at 12pm, with DJs from 1pm and live entertainment from 5pm on both days. Entry was one-in-one-out when it reached capacity, so arrive early to guarantee a good spot.

How to book your room early

  1. Decide whether you want a hotel with a bar, a guest house or a men-only stay. See Pride weekend hotels.
  2. Choose somewhere near Lord Street so the street party and the parade are minutes away. The full stays list has locations.
  3. Contact the hotel directly as soon as dates are announced and ask about minimum stays.
  4. Check cancellation terms before paying.

What else is on around Pride?

Many venues put on extra shows and parties across the weekend, so it is worth looking at both the what's on guide and nightlife near your hotel before you arrive. Funny Girls, on Dickson Road, plus the bars along Queen Street are all within a short walk of Lord Street.

Check each venue for listed hours and ticket details, since they are often different on Pride weekend.

Do I need to book a hotel for Pride weekend?

Yes, and as soon as you can. Pride is the busiest weekend of the LGBTQ+ calendar in the resort, and the places closest to Lord Street are the first to go. Booking early gives you the widest choice, from men-only hotels to gay-owned guest houses.

Tips for a smooth weekend

  • Arrive early on the day if you want to get into the street party, because entry was one-in-one-out when full.
  • Wear comfortable shoes, as you will be on your feet and walking the Prom.
  • Take water, sun cream or a coat, depending on the forecast.
  • Agree a meeting point with your group in case you get separated.
  • Keep your hotel name and address saved on your phone.

Staying safe and getting around

Weekends are busy, and transport can differ from normal timetables, so check on the day. Read our safety guide for hate crime reporting and practical tips, and see what is on for shows around Pride. For history and support services, try rainbowquarter.co.uk.

safety.title: Safety and Getting Back to Your Hotel | Blackpool.gay
safety.description: Safety tips for LGBTQ+ visitors in Blackpool: how to report hate crime, where to find support on Dickson Road, and how to plan your walk back to your room.
safety.h1: Staying safe and getting back to your hotel in Blackpool
safety.intro: Practical advice for LGBTQ+ visitors on planning your journey home, reporting hate crime and finding support if a night out goes wrong.
safety.body:
Most visitors have a great time in Blackpool. A little planning makes it better, and it helps to know where to turn if something goes wrong.

Where do I report hate crime when visiting Blackpool?

Lancashire Constabulary has a hate crime page encouraging anyone who experiences hostility motivated by hate to report it, and it links a Hate Crime Victim Care Pack. Check the page directly for the current online form and contact options at lancashire.police.uk. In an emergency, or if someone is in danger, call 999.

Lancashire Victim Services offers free, confidential support on 0300 323 0085, from 9am to 6:30pm Monday to Friday.

Where can I get LGBTQ+ support locally?

Renaissance UK is a charity with an office at 102 Dickson Road, FY1 2BU, listed as open Monday to Friday, 9 to 5. It runs sexual health support, social and support groups and HIV and syphilis drop-in testing. Confirm opening hours before you visit. For a wider list of services, see rainbowquarter.co.uk.

What is Be Who You Want To Be?

It is a Blackpool Council campaign and action plan for the Claremont area, agreed on 22 January 2024 and aimed at making the area safe for everyone. Partners include Renaissance, Blackpool Pride and the hoteliers group BAGS. Rainbow crossings on Dickson Road were part of it.

Practical night tips

  • Choose a hotel close to the bars so you can walk back. The stays near Queen Street and our full list show distances.
  • Agree a meeting point and share your hotel name and address with friends.
  • Keep your phone charged and save your hotel's number.
  • Stay with people you trust and look out for each other.
  • Book a licensed taxi through a reputable firm or ask your venue to arrange one. Avoid unlicensed offers.
  • Check train and tram times with National Rail Enquiries and Blackpool Transport on the day, as late services can differ, especially on Pride weekends.

Planning the walk back

The simplest safety measure is a hotel close to where you will be. Many stays are a short walk from Funny Girls, Queen Street and the bars on Dickson Road, so you may not need a taxi at all. Our walking times are measured from the owner's own coordinates, and each listing shows how far you are from the action.

Before you go out, look up the route in daylight if you can, and stick to busy, well-lit streets when you walk home. If a place does not feel right, trust your instincts and go somewhere else.

Looking after your friends

Agree before you go who is going home with whom. Check in with each other during the night, and never leave a friend alone who has had too much to drink. If someone is unwell or you are worried about their safety, ask venue staff for help or call 999.

Drink and personal belongings

  • Keep an eye on your drink and do not accept drinks from strangers you do not know.
  • Keep valuables out of sight and your bag zipped or closed.
  • Take a spare payment card or some cash in a separate pocket.
  • Know the name of your hotel and save its phone number.

If you have been targeted

You are not to blame for what happened, and you do not have to cope alone. Contact the police, Lancashire Victim Services or a support service as soon as you feel able. Even if you decide not to go further, telling someone you trust can help.

Other places to look

Return to nightlife near your hotel, check what is open tonight, or talk to other visitors on the community board, including a thread about getting home late.

forum.title: Gay Blackpool Community Board | Blackpool.gay
forum.description: Ask other LGBTQ+ travellers where to stay, eat and go in Blackpool. A friendly, pre-moderated community board for planning your gay weekend away.
forum.intro: A friendly place to ask other LGBTQ+ travellers about hotels, nights out and getting home, with every post checked before it appears.
forum.body:
Planning a trip is easier when you can ask people who have done it. The community board is where visitors and locals share tips on where to stay, where to eat and how to enjoy Blackpool.

How the board works

Every post is checked by a moderator before it appears. That keeps the board friendly and useful, and it means your message may take a little while to show up.

Topics to start with

  • New to the forum? Say hello
  • First time in the Rainbow Quarter
  • Monday to Wednesday in Blackpool
  • Where do you eat before a night out?
  • Getting home late from Queen Street
  • Where to stay: quiet B&B or a hotel with a bar?

Community guidelines

Be kind, keep it relevant and respect other people's privacy. Do not share personal details. For safety information and reporting hate crime, see our safety page. If you need somewhere to stay, start with the stays directory.

about.title: About Blackpool.gay: A Stay-First Guide | Blackpool.gay
about.description: Blackpool.gay is an independent, stay-first guide for LGBTQ+ visitors. Find out how we check our facts, how to send corrections and who we are.
about.intro: Blackpool.gay is an independent guide to staying, planning and enjoying a gay weekend in Blackpool, with accommodation first and nightlife second.
about.body:
Blackpool.gay exists to help LGBTQ+ visitors pick a good base and plan a great trip. We start with where you will sleep, then look at what is happening nearby.

Who runs this site?

It is an independent project, not affiliated with any hotel, bar or venue. We are not paid to rank places, and we say plainly when something is unconfirmed.

How do we check our facts?

  • Names, addresses and walking times come from the owner's own records and coordinates.
  • Other details come from published sources such as council pages, local news and venue websites.
  • Where a detail cannot be verified, we leave it out or say so.
  • Hours and prices change, so we ask you to confirm them with the venue.

Found a mistake?

Email hello@blackpool.gay and we will check and correct it. Hotel and venue owners are welcome to get in touch with updates.

Why stay-first?

Most guides begin with the bars. We think a good trip begins with a good room, because it decides how far you walk, how late you stay out and how comfortable your weekend feels. Nightlife is a close second, and we cover it as "what is near your hotel".

What we are not

We are not a booking agent, and we cannot guarantee that a hotel will meet your needs. Always read the hotel's own details and contact it directly before booking. We do not make up reviews, ratings or prices, and we do not display accreditations unless they are confirmed.

Take part

Join the community board to share tips with other visitors, or read about Blackpool Pride if you are planning your trip around it.

Sister site

For venue history, performer profiles and support services, visit our sister site, rainbowquarter.co.uk. Back here, start with where to stay, then see what is on and our safety guide.
